key_insight: Sequential hot rotary swaging in the β and α+β phase fields refined Zr-4Nb-2Al microstructure and developed fibre textures, while subsequent α+β deformation traded compressive yield strength for greater plastic deformability.
engineering_relevance: Phase-field-controlled swaging offers a route to tailor strength, deformability, and radial hardness uniformity in dual-phase zirconium alloy rods.
method: Use electrical resistivity measurements to select β-field processing at 880°C and α+β processing at 780°C.
Apply induction-assisted rotary swaging with thermographic temperature control, reducing rod diameter from 12 to 6.3 mm.
Track microstructure, crystallographic texture, phase constitution, and mechanical response through sequential deformation.
evidence_signal: At 72% total area reduction, prior-β grains refined to approximately 100 µm; subsequent α+β swaging reduced compressive yield strength from 1103 to 839 MPa, with maximum fracture strain reaching 32%.
watch_item: The abstract reports compression performance only; tensile, fatigue, and service-environment behaviour remain unestablished.
paper_title: Evolution of microstructure and crystallographic texture in a novel Zr-4Nb-2Al alloy during hot rotary swaging
